title: Report isolated worker failures without waiting for earlier modules
body:
A later parallel unittest worker can fail unexpectedly while an earlier module remains blocked. `ThreadPoolExecutor.map` hides that exception in input order, delaying the existing owned-process cleanup until the earlier module finishes or reaches its deadline.

This observes completed futures immediately and still returns ordinary result rows in the requested input order. It preserves the original exception object, handles worker `StopIteration` separately from completion-iterator exhaustion, retains protected SIGTERM waits, and continues collecting ordinary nonzero unittest results. Existing process registration, cleanup and queue-cancellation mechanisms stay in place.

Three substantive commits retain the failing regression, minimal repair with exception/receipt controls, and the behavior/evidence note. The controller-cancellation fixture submits both active and queued futures before injecting its exception, preserving its actual queue coverage.

**Validation:** CPython 3.12.7 / macOS 27.0 arm64, normal and optimized, warnings as errors:

- Eight new methods pass: real later pipe/cleanup errors with four native-observed processes, exact exception identity, worker `StopIteration`/`SystemExit`, retained KeyboardInterrupt/RuntimeError plus queued work, reversed completion with exact NUL-containing stdout, ordinary failure continuation, and an ordered-wait mutant that must fail. Both actual owned groups must exit before independent teardown.
- Existing isolated-test group: 50 cases with 23 platform skips, both modes pass. Existing SIGTERM 11 and POSIX-pipe 10 methods pass in both modes.
- A seven-file exact committed export, read-only and without Git metadata, passes the optimized eight-method regression (5.665 s); archive SHA-256 `6210ae471b2deccf4003836578638766c2b81bfe55d52a0d76f29d5f8d91e1a0`.
- Both unchanged registered `isolated-test-bytecode` and `isolated-descendant-bytecode` hooks pass, including source/cache and mutation controls (6.552 / 25.087 s).
- Before repair, the initial five-method regression has two real failure cases; both wait for forced release. A separate two-worker control changed from 4.033 s/forced release to 0.198 s/no forced release; these are local observations, not latency guarantees.

**Known baseline failures, kept explicit:** the broader historical-completion group has the same sixteen failing subtest keys on patched code and an export of sixteen exact canonical-base inputs. Both reject `scripts/partial_swap/shared.py` at the source guard before historical child execution. The actual CI package plan selects three packages; the third, `isolated-runner-successor`, rejects `certificates/selected-result.json` at metadata validation. Exact-base/current checker comparisons reproduce that same first rejection with unchanged guard inputs. No frozen source, accepted hash or selected record is repinned. This PR does not claim complete CI success or a full historical replay.

The new regression is included by the existing hosted `test_research_*.py` onboarding pattern. Native Windows execution remains unrun; the hosted Linux result below supplements the local checkpoint. Queued-launch cancellation is guaranteed after the controller observes the abort and takes its existing registration lock; work may start before that observation. Detached process sessions remain outside the ownership contract.

[Source-pinned behavior, commands and open next questions](docs/research/isolated-worker-failfast.md) · [Canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1472#discussioncomment-19139343). Base `bee95ce88f9f19802f0613f92838895cd0e14a1f`, priority revision 7. No mathematical or selected-frontier claim.

**Hosted CI verified (2026-10-23T06:44:19.824960+00:00): three successful checks, one failed check; CI remains red.** The [Ubuntu 24.04.5 / CPython 3.12.15 plan/onboarding job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39911801256/job/120276271364) logs all eight new worker-failure methods as `ok`; its complete onboarding run reports 387 tests in 140.015 s, with 11 skips. Both registered bytecode/descendant replay jobs also succeeded.

The [failed isolated-runner-successor job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39911801256/job/120277480937) stops at `working source drift: certificates/selected-result.json` before its registered commands run. This exactly matches the already reproduced canonical-base metadata rejection. The job checks out GitHub merge `665e7bc0e786cd4ea559bb295ea3f60f70b393c5` (submitted head `baab49ce64e6c170ad74432992a35a9c4a54be92` into `f259dabc7d70e0db8d6d36bfda888f008bbfecc1`). Seven direct source comparisons verify that this checkout's checker, rejected selected record and successor metadata are byte-identical to canonical `bee95ce88f9f19802f0613f92838895cd0e14a1f`, while its runner and new regression bytes are identical to the submitted head. The failure classification therefore uses actual logs and source identity. No historical scientific replay, source-pin rewrite, native Windows result or hosted optimized new-test run is claimed.

Credit Nick Petalas, Paul Romeo, yssite, ywz65, Mihir Srivastava, Douglas Colkitt and the retained isolation/cancellation/source contributors, including JoyboyBrian's #4779/#4975. Scientific source base `bee95ce88f9f19802f0613f92838895cd0e14a1f` is intentionally retained; changed paths are disjoint. Refreshed overlap covered 304 open PRs and 4,114 discussions; local inventory covers all 6,690 notes at the scientific base. Coverage is advisory, not a novelty certificate.
